# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 9 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 9 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_009_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 1

**1** Here is the third vision I received, my friends. **2** I had been fasting repeatedly, asking God to show me what he had promised through the elderly woman. That same night she appeared and said: "You are so persistent in your eagerness to understand — good. Come to the field where you farm, around the fifth hour, and I will meet you there and show you what you need to see." **3** "Which part of the field?" I asked. "Wherever you choose — just find a quiet spot." Then, before I could even tell her where, she added, "I'll find you wherever you are." **4** I went to the field, friends, carefully counted off the hours, and came to the spot I had in mind. There I found an ivory couch with a linen pillow on it and a fine linen covering laid over it. **5** No one was there — just the couch. I was flooded with awe. I trembled and my hair stood on end. I steadied myself. Then I saw the old woman coming toward me, carrying a book. She sat down and said to me: "Hello, man of God." I started crying — I couldn't help it. **6** "Why are you crying?" she asked. "Because I'm not sure I have what it takes to make it to the end," I said. She replied, "God himself has placed you here to endure the trials of this world — for your own sake and for your family's. So be brave." **7** "Show me the vision, please," I said. "Right now?" she asked. "Yes — I'm longing to see it." She reached out and touched me, and the moment she did I felt completely fresh — as if I had just stepped out of a bath. **8** "Come," she said. And there before me were the same things I had glimpsed before: the great tower, being built with brilliant squared stones.

---

*PNEUMA note: The physical refreshment at the elderly woman's touch (v.7) is a purifying experience — perhaps echoing baptismal renewal, making Hermas ready to receive the vision.*
